title: Graph Engineering: Make Agent Structure Explicit

questions.question: Which four parts make an agent graph reviewable?
options: Nodes, edges, shared state, and routing rules
Prompts, temperature, tokens, and model size
A dashboard, a queue, a database, and a webhook
One loop, one prompt, one tool, and one model
questions.explanation: The graph makes responsibilities, handoffs, durable data, and next-step decisions explicit.

questions.question: What should happen when a verifier returns an unknown route label?
options: Fall back silently to merge
Treat it as a pass because the node completed
Fail closed and surface a graph error
Delete the verifier result
questions.explanation: Unknown routing is a graph-definition failure. Silent success would turn a malformed decision into an unsafe side effect.

questions.question: Why does the reference graph deep-copy state before each fan-out branch?
options: To let branches mutate one another faster
To keep branch inputs isolated so their patches can be merged deliberately
To avoid recording branch outputs
To make all branches share a hidden transcript
questions.explanation: Isolation prevents one branch from accidentally changing another branch's input before fan-in.

questions.question: What does the approval node do when no human decision is present?
options: Pause and persist an approval request
Assume approval after one retry
Route directly to merge
Discard the state and restart at research
questions.explanation: Missing approval is not consent. The graph pauses, checkpoints state, and resumes only after an explicit decision.

questions.question: When should a failed verification route back to research instead of implementation?
options: Whenever implementation takes more than one round
When the requirements or evidence needed to implement are insufficient
When the approval node is paused
When a branch produced a list
questions.explanation: Rollback should target the layer that owns the defect; missing requirements belong to research, not guesswork in implementation.

questions.question: What is the safest fan-in behavior for conflicting scalar updates from parallel branches?
options: Use whichever branch finishes last
Concatenate the scalar values into a string
Raise a conflict and require an explicit merge decision
Drop both values and continue
questions.explanation: A silent overwrite destroys provenance. The runner rejects conflicting scalar updates so a human or merge rule can decide.
